question: What is the primary goal of the Essential Drug Programme?

options.A: Eliminating all herbal remedies from clinical practice
options.B: Promoting the most expensive imported drug brands
options.C: Ensuring availability and affordability of safe medicines
options.D: Maximizing profits for private pharmaceutical importers

explanation: The programme focuses on making effective and safe treatments accessible and financially viable for populations. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why does the health system restrict the number of pharmaceutical variants stocked?

options.A: To stop doctors from prescribing any medications at all
options.B: To prevent wasteful spending on redundant or ineffective products
options.C: To guarantee higher taxes on imported medical supplies
options.D: To reduce the total number of patients visiting government hospitals

explanation: Limiting choices to proven medications optimizes limited health budgets and simplifies supply management. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h1)

question: When did the World Health Organization publish the first model list of essential medicines?
explanation: The inaugural WHO expert committee list of essential medicines was published in 1977. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h2)

question: How often does the WHO update its model list of essential medicines?
explanation: Biennial updates allow the WHO list to incorporate new therapeutic discoveries and changing disease trends. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which factor is NOT one of the core pillars of the essential drugs concept?
explanation: Appearance and packaging do not determine a medicine's essential clinical value or safety profile. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h3)

question: What does the relevance principle require when choosing essential medicines?

options.A: Selection based purely on international popularity
options.B: Preference for remedies requested by private marketers
options.C: Inclusion of every newly invented molecule on earth
options.D: Alignment with local disease patterns and health needs

explanation: Medicines are chosen because they directly target the actual illnesses affecting the local population. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h3)

question: Who conducts the evaluation and selection of medicines for national formularies?
explanation: Clinical and public health experts review trial data and cost analyses to select safe and effective drugs. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h4)

question: What is the main benefit of standardizing medication formulations in a health system?

options.A: Eliminating the need for any laboratory testing facilities
options.B: Increasing the financial cost of running public pharmacies
options.C: Allowing patients to buy any foreign brand they prefer
options.D: Reducing dispensing errors and simplifying adverse reaction monitoring

explanation: Using standard formulations makes it easier for staff to manage stock and track patient safety. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h4)

question: What document guides pharmaceutical procurement and health insurance reimbursement in Nigeria?
explanation: The NEML is the authoritative guide for public sector drug procurement and insurance coverage. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h5)

question: Why are certain complex medicines restricted to tertiary health facilities in Nigeria?

options.A: Because those facilities have the necessary specialist support and diagnostic tools
options.B: Because tertiary hospitals charge less money for imported drugs
options.C: To prevent primary healthcare workers from ever learning about pharmacology
options.D: To make sure rural patients never gain access to modern healthcare

explanation: Advanced therapies require specialized monitoring and diagnostic equipment typically found only in higher-level centers. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h5)

question: What inventory control approach involves reordering based on actual consumption data?
explanation: The pull system relies on consumption rates at the facility level to drive replenishment quantities. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h6)

question: What is a common consequence of poor cold-chain storage in public health supply chains?

options.A: Loss of potency in vaccines and thermolabile medications
options.B: Automatic improvement of drug expiration dates
options.C: Faster delivery times to remote primary health clinics
options.D: Increased financial profit for local retail pharmacies

explanation: Temperature-sensitive drugs degrade quickly when cold-chain protocols are broken during storage or transport. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h6)

question: Which Nigerian agency conducts post-market surveillance to combat falsified medications?
explanation: NAFDAC regulates and controls drug manufacturing, importation, distribution, and sales in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h7)

question: What is a direct consequence of the widespread irrational use of broad-spectrum antibiotics?
explanation: Overusing or misusing antibiotics accelerates the survival of resistant microbial strains in the community. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h7)

question: What is a primary nursing responsibility related to hospital ward medications?

options.A: Monitoring stock levels and verifying adherence to the NEML
options.B: Formulating national health insurance reimbursement laws
options.C: Importing raw chemical compounds from overseas manufacturers
options.D: Determining the wholesale market price of new drugs

explanation: Nurses manage ward inventory and ensure administered drugs match authorized essential lists. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h8)

question: How do bedside nurses contribute directly to national pharmacovigilance?

options.A: By preventing patients from asking questions about their treatment
options.B: By manufacturing replacement herbal extracts in the ward utility room
options.C: By locking all medication cabinets permanently against doctors
options.D: By reporting observed adverse drug reactions to appropriate authorities

explanation: Nurses observe patients closely after administration, making them key reporters of unexpected side effects. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T3#GNS215_U1_T3_h8)
